title: Maths Knowledge Graph finite notation registry
description: Reference structural schema for author-approved notation registry version 1. Native validation additionally checks declared public concept identities and exact scopes, unique profile/variant keys, a declared default, complete role placeholders in identical order, safe nonbinding TeX and equal operation-token counts. These checks do not prove mathematical equivalence. This schema is not automatically registered with the Quarto editor. Whole-file native limits are 2 MiB and 64 JSON nesting levels; duplicate decoded mapping keys are refused.
$comment: Native text bounds are UTF-8 bytes, whereas JSON Schema maxLength counts Unicode code points. Runtime validation remains authoritative, particularly for non-ASCII text and semantic cross-record constraints. Registry values are literal JSON, not Markdown metadata.

profiles.description: May be empty. Profile IDs must be unique; no public/private eligibility is inferred from an ID or spelling.

literal.description: Nonblank literal single-line text. JSON values are not parsed as Markdown.

conceptIdentity.description: An HTTP(S) identity or a namespace-qualified compact identity declared in the catalogue. Native validation expands namespaces and requires a supported HTTP(S) URI without credentials, then looks up an explicitly public concept. This schema alone cannot establish that lookup.

scope.description: Must match the referenced public concept's catalogue scope exactly.

roles.description: Free argument roles, each used exactly once as {{role}} in every variant. All variants preserve role order; binding expressions are unsupported.

default.description: Must equal one declared variant ID within this profile.

variants.description: Variant IDs are unique within the profile. Author approval is not independent proof of semantic equivalence.

tex.description: Finite nonbinding TeX using declared {{role}} placeholders, approved operator/grouping commands, optional literal operatorname, digits and supported punctuation. Native validation rejects free literal variables, active TeX, undeclared/binding commands, repeated/missing roles, changed role order, unmatched braces and differing explicit operation-token counts.
